clue.text: My American off-road vehicle about to go over loose rocks through sierra

parts.note: a Jeep is a rugged off-road car

indicators.note: going over turns a short word head over heels, so its letters are read backwards

parts.note: RE means about or concerning
scree is loose stones on a slope
per means through or by means of
Sierra is S in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone drives an off-road vehicle over loose rocks in a mountain range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to go over' is one piece of wordplay: the word for about, flipped. 'Through' is the Latin-derived PER.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeepers creepers is an old American exclamation of surprise, like 'my!' or 'my goodness!'.

clue.text: Converted Joshua Tree fans embracing unknown saviour

indicators.note: embracing means holding something inside, so one piece goes within the others
something converted has been changed into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for the rearrangement
Z is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Fans of U2's album The Joshua Tree are converted to Christianity.
explanation.walkthrough: Joshua Tree is both a desert park and U2's 1987 album, which helps the fans sound natural.
explanation.definitionFit: Christians regard Jesus of Nazareth as the saviour of mankind, a title used of him throughout the New Testament.

clue.text: Ascendant Gulf state Europe embraces, showing charm

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold inside, so the first word goes within the second

parts.note: EUR is an abbreviation for Europe

indicators.note: in a down clue something ascending travels upwards, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: Oman is a state on the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea

explanation.surface: A rising Gulf state, taken in by Europe, proves alluring.
explanation.definitionFit: To enamour is to fill with love, which is what a charm does when it captivates someone.

clue.text: Using which dials may be adjusted on screen

definitions.text: Using which dials may be adjusted on screen

parts.words: dials may be adjusted on screen
parts.note: surface reading: a tool for tuning instrument dials shown on a monitor
setter's reading: dial is slang for face, so faces are pieced together on a computer

explanation.surface: Some software lets you tweak the dials displayed on a screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dial' is British slang for a face; police build suspects' faces on screen with this system.
explanation.definitionFit: An E-FIT is a computer-generated facial composite of a suspect, assembled from witness descriptions by adjusting features.

clue.text: Gloom ultimately depresses 1960s band

parts.note: shadow is darkness or gloom

indicators.note: ultimately points to what comes at the end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: final letter of depresses

explanation.surface: Gloom eventually brings down a group from the sixties.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shadows were Cliff Richard's backing group and a hit instrumental band of the 1960s.

clue.text: Illustrator's stress precedes overacting

parts.note: to rack is to strain or stress
ham acting is overacting

explanation.surface: An illustrator's anxiety comes before some theatrical overacting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'precedes' just places one piece before the other; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Rackham was a celebrated English book illustrator of fairy tales and Peter Pan.

clue.text: Maybe female from Cotswolds goes on river vessel

parts.note: a Cotswold is a breed of sheep, and the female of it is a ewe
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A woman from the Cotswolds boards a river boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cotswolds are hills in England, but Cotswold is also a sheep breed. 'goes on' just attaches the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large jug or pitcher, a kind of vessel for holding water.

clue.text: Version of Usenet I linked to facilities?

indicators.note: a version is a different rendering, so the letters appear in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A version of the Usenet discussion system I linked to other services.
explanation.definitionFit: An en suite bedroom has its bathroom attached, so it is connected to the facilities.

clue.text: Excellent reception from van doing broadcast in depot

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the word for the depot

parts.note: a station is a depot, as for buses or trains

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: An outside-broadcast van at a depot gets a terrific welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: A standing ovation, where the audience rises to applaud, is the warmest reception a performer can get.

clue.text: Draws back, lacking electronic energy

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word from its end to its start
lacking means going without, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: to animate is to draw cartoon films
E is the abbreviation for electronic, the letter removed

explanation.surface: Someone retreats because they have no electronic power left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draws back' looks like one verb meaning withdraws; split it, so 'Draws' is a word for animating cartoons and 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is staying power, the physical energy that keeps a person going.

clue.text: Side show location

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the London district hosting the annual flower show

explanation.walkthrough: 'Side show' reads as a fairground attraction; split it into a team and a show's venue.
explanation.definitionFit: Chelsea is a London football club and the setting of the RHS Chelsea Flower Show each May.

clue.text: Rat on small skip

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
to hop is to skip or jump

explanation.surface: A rodent sitting on a little rubbish skip.
explanation.walkthrough: A skip is a British builder's rubbish container, which sets up the rat picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop someone is British slang for informing on them to the police, just as rat on does.

clue.text: Commotion from adult by back-to-back houses

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house

indicators.note: back-to-back means a copy faces the other way, so the second one is read backwards

parts.note: the second house, turned to face the first
A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A row breaks out over an adult living next to terraced back-to-back houses.
explanation.walkthrough: Back-to-back houses are terraced homes sharing a rear wall, common in northern English cities; here they are HO and its mirror image.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoo-ha is an informal word for a fuss or commotion.

clue.text: Turn large sailing ship, missing source of blockage?

indicators.note: missing means without, so part of the word is taken away

parts.note: a windjammer was a large merchant sailing ship
a jammer is something that blocks radio signals

explanation.surface: A big sailing ship turns, apparently lacking whatever was blocking it.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind is to turn or twist, as in winding a handle or a road that winds.

clue.text: Lout cycles on middle of triangular decking

indicators.note: cycles means the letters go round, with the last moving to the front

parts.note: an oik is a British slang word for a lout

indicators.note: middle of keeps only the central letters of the following word

parts.note: the two central letters of triangular

explanation.surface: A yob cycles across a triangular wooden deck.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck someone is to knock them down, and KO-ing means knocking someone out.

clue.text: 27 from Quebec entering near-perfect set of grades?

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one letter is placed within the other piece

parts.note: all top marks but one, a single B among the As
Quebec is Q in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Something from Quebec enters an almost flawless school report.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 refers to the answer at 27-down, CITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Aqaba is a port city in Jordan on the Red Sea, so it is an example of a city.

clue.text: Head of Unit Four is exceptionally violent

indicators.note: exceptionally suggests something out of the ordinary, so the letters are put out of order
the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of Unit
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The leader of Unit Four is unusually aggressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' looks like a link to the definition, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Furious can describe something wild and violent, like a furious storm, as well as anger.

clue.text: Perhaps Alexander's soldiers entertaining question in church

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to have them in, so one piece holds the rest

parts.note: men are soldiers, the other ranks

indicators.note: in places the question abbreviation inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
QU is an abbreviation for question

explanation.surface: Alexander the Great's troops take a question into a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alexander's soldiers' suggests the Macedonian army, but Alexander McQueen was a British fashion designer; the 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander McQueen was a famous designer, so the surname McQueen fits him as one example of the name.

clue.text: Register watercourse crossing minute area from the east

indicators.note: in an across clue reading from the east means right to left
a waterway crossing something spans it, so the letter sits inside the waterway

parts.note: a canal is an artificial watercourse
M is the abbreviation for minute
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A record notes a stream passing through a tiny area on the eastern side.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is an annual book of records and data, so it is a kind of register.

clue.text: Dodgy guys regularly claim having problem with beef?

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable or crooked, so the letters are jumbled
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: first and third letters of guys
taken as written

explanation.surface: Shady characters make a claim about a dispute over beef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beef' looks like meat or a grievance; here it is slang for muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: Myalgic means relating to muscle pain, and beef is informal for brawn or muscle.

clue.text: Fop, 90, residing in valley

indicators.note: residing in means living inside, so one piece is housed within the other

parts.note: a coomb, or combe, is a short valley
XC is 90 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A dandy aged ninety lives in a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A coxcomb is an old word for a vain, showy man, the same as a fop or dandy.

clue.text: Plant automatic software for backing up half of financial statements

indicators.note: backing up means moving in reverse, so the word goes backwards

parts.note: a bot is a software program that runs automatically

indicators.note: half of tells us to keep one half and drop the rest

parts.note: accounts are financial statements

explanation.surface: Install automated software to back up half a company's financial reports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing up' sounds like making a copy of files; here it reverses the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobacco is the plant whose leaves are dried for smoking.

clue.text: Tense cad, a bit of a swine

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
a rotter is a cad, a man who behaves badly

explanation.surface: An anxious cad who is somewhat of a swine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swine' seems to describe the cad; it is literal, a pig.
explanation.definitionFit: A trotter is a pig's foot, so it is one part of a swine.

clue.text: Pizzas variable in state close to Italy

indicators.note: in puts the variable inside the string that follows it

parts.note: Cal. is an abbreviation for California
Z is an algebraic variable
on can mean close to, as in a town on the coast
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Pizzas vary from region to region near Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: The variable goes in among the other pieces, between the state and the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Calzoni is the plural of calzone, a folded, stuffed pizza.

clue.text: Hero for the most part not to cross

indicators.note: for the most part means mostly, not entirely, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a door that is to is closed, so one not to is ajar
an X is a cross

explanation.surface: A hero who mostly refuses to cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' here is the adverb for a door being shut, as in 'pull the door to'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ajax was a mighty Greek hero of the Trojan War.

clue.text: Former old Liberal accepts ultimate in faint praise

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the letter goes inside the others

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: ultimate in points to the last letter of the next word

parts.note: last letter of faint
O is the abbreviation for old
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A former Liberal politician gets only faint praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faint praise' reads as one phrase; split it so praise is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly.

clue.text: Minuscule jumper, formerly two bob (reduced) each

parts.note: FL is the abbreviation for florin, an old British two-shilling coin
EA is the abbreviation for each

explanation.surface: A tiny sweater once cost two shillings each, marked down.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is British for a sweater, a false lead; and two bob meant two shillings, the value of a florin.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea is a tiny insect famous for jumping huge distances relative to its size.

clue.text: Ring phone engineer that's late

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a call, as in 'give me a ring'
second meaning: the inventor of the telephone, now dead

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a phone repairman running late; 'late' means deceased.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell is a call on the phone in British slang, and Alexander Graham Bell was the late telephone pioneer.

clue.text: Bath, possibly extremely comfy, inspiring hanky-panky

indicators.note: inspiring literally means breathing in, so one piece is drawn inside the other
extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of comfy
it is slang for sex

explanation.surface: A very comfortable bath encourages some hanky-panky.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is a city in Somerset, England, not a tub.
explanation.definitionFit: Bath is an example of a city, hence the 'possibly'.

clue.text: Composer ignoring a novelist and artist

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: Edward Elgar was an English composer
the letter to be left out
Umberto Eco was an Italian novelist

explanation.surface: A composer overlooks a novelist and a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: El Greco was a Greek-born Spanish Renaissance painter.

clue.text: Polish capital

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., a fine abrasive powder used for polishing
second meaning: the capital city of Libya

explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish capital' points to Warsaw; read polish with a small p, a cleaning compound.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is a rottenstone powder used as a polishing agent and also the capital of Libya.

clue.text: Work by E L Kirchner with fun flourishes

indicators.note: flourishes are showy twirls, so the letters are swirled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painting by the Expressionist E L Kirchner has playful flourishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' looks like a link to the artist but belongs in the fodder; Ernst Ludwig Kirchner was a German painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Adventures of Huckleberry Finn is Mark Twain's novel, a literary work.
